## TL;DR

Round 2 fixes the review's blocking CSS-cascade bug and the follow-up edge cases
for task #1152. The narrow-screen "Preview Build" hide rule is now
`.topbar .preview-build-banner`, so it wins by specificity instead of losing to
the later base rule. The login screen's existing RepoOS mark is now the same
one-action return when a Hub token is remembered, covering an expired session.
The logo tap probes the landing page with a short deadline and falls back to an
in-memory `blob:` document on the same origin, so an unreachable server no
longer leaves the WebView open. The shell's navigation handler moved into
`src/core/hub-return.ts` and has a real effect-level unit test instead of only a
regex over `mobile/src/browser.ts`. The 44px logo hit box now uses `-6px`
inline margins, matching the phone gap, so it no longer overlaps its neighbour.
Shots were re-declared at 360px dark and 390px light plus desktop. The web UI
and mobile `www` bundles build; the affected Vitest suites pass. `repoos check`
is green apart from the gate's remote-runner test skip, which I covered by
running the affected suites directly.

## Work and rationale

The core architecture is unchanged: the connected server runs in an isolated
WebView with no Capacitor bridge, so the only native request it can make is
"dismiss this browser and show the picker". The shell opens each server with a
fresh `?repoos_hub=<token>`; the SPA navigates to
`/__repoos_hub/return-to-picker#hub-return=<token>`; and the shell's existing
`browserPageNavigationCompleted` listener accepts only an exact origin, path
and token before closing. The fragment keeps the token out of the HTTP request.

The review's blocking bug was pure cascade order: the hide rule sat near the
top of the narrow-screen block while the base `.preview-build-banner` rule is
thousands of lines later with equal specificity. I scoped the narrow rule to
`.topbar .preview-build-banner`, which raises specificity and cannot be
defeated by later source order. I also verified the built stylesheet: the
selector appears inside the 719.98px media query, and the base rule remains
unchanged for wider screens. A static test now asserts the scoped selector so
this exact regression is caught.

For the expired-session edge case, `LoginView` reads the same hub session at
setup. Its existing 44px login logo becomes a button with an explicit
"Return to RepoOS Hub server picker" label when a token is present; otherwise
it remains the decorative mark. That matters because `/login` renders without
`TopBar`, so the top-left return affordance does not exist there. The token is
remembered in `sessionStorage` by `claimHubContext()` before the router mounts,
so an expired session mid-use still has it when the login view appears. For a
cold unauthenticated open, `readHubShellSession` also reads the token from the
server's `/login?redirect=` target, so the same login mark works there.

For an unreachable server, the previous design relied on the landing page
loading so the shell would see a completed navigation. I added a short,
abortable `fetch` probe of the landing page (`redirect: "manual"`, 1.2s
deadline). If the probe succeeds, the normal same-origin navigation is used.
If it fails, the SPA creates an in-memory `blob:` HTML document and navigates
to `<blob-url>#hub-return=<token>`. A blob URL needs no network and keeps the
server origin, so the shell's origin and token checks still hold. The fallback
page is script-free and includes an absolute link back to the server in case
the shell cannot react. I kept the server landing route because it is the
normal, most predictable path and gives the WebView a real page.

I also moved the per-navigation decision into `applyHubNavigation()` in
`src/core/hub-return.ts`. `mobile/src/browser.ts` now only supplies the
effects: null the session, close the InAppBrowser, and forward normal
navigations. The new unit test exercises undefined URLs, ordinary navigation,
and a matching return in one pass, so the close path is tested rather than
merely grepped.

The phone layout remains: the chip keeps the project name, the branch glyph is
hidden, the name ellipsizes inside a `min-width: 0` flexible wrapper, and
search is a fixed 44x44 icon button with an `aria-label`. The preview marker is
hidden below 720px because it is developer chrome and otherwise consumes the
width the name needs. Colour-picker semantics are unchanged.

## Approaches tried

I considered making the logo return a `blob:` navigation in every case, which
would remove the network step and the server route entirely. I rejected it as
the primary path because a normal same-origin document navigation is the
best-tested behavior in the WebView plugin, and the landing page gives a
clearer failure page. Using the blob only after a failed probe keeps the
common path conventional while making the offline case work.

I considered moving the preview-banner hide rule to the end of `style.css`
instead of raising specificity. Scoping it to `.topbar` is more local and
self-documenting, and it cannot regress if the stylesheet is reordered again.

For the login screen, I considered adding a separate floating "Back to
servers" button. Reusing the existing login logo is less visual noise and
preserves the screen's current composition; it only gains button semantics
when the Hub token is present.

I also considered leaving the offline case as a documented limitation. Since
the review explicitly named it and the WebView has no visible close control in
the chromeless configuration, a fallback was worth the small probe delay.

## Challenges and blockers

- The WebView plugin exposes only completed navigation events, not navigation
  starts or failures. The probe is the practical way to distinguish "the
  landing page will load" from "the server is unreachable" before deciding
  which navigation to perform.
- A login redirect is treated as unhealthy by the probe (`redirect: "manual"`),
  so the fallback is used rather than leaving the WebView on a login screen
  that has no return affordance.
- The scoped `repoos check` still reports the test step as skipped
  (`REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1`) because a remote validation runner owns it. I ran the
  twelve affected/adjacent Vitest files directly; all 126 tests passed.
- No real Android or iOS device was available. The native handler now has a
  real unit test, and both the web UI and mobile `www` bundles were rebuilt,
  but the final on-device close behavior should still be confirmed in review.
  The blob fallback's navigation event is the least-exercised path here.
- The initial `?repoos_hub=` token still reaches server/proxy logs. It is not a
  credential and only permits closing that WebView; the return hop uses the
  fragment. I left that as accepted low-impact behavior.

## Key learnings

- CSS specificity is the right fix for a narrow-screen override that must beat
  a later base rule; relying on source position inside a 13k-line stylesheet is
  how the original bug slipped through. Check the built stylesheet, not only
  the source file.
- A native shell affordance has to exist on the login screen too. An expired
  session is exactly when a one-action exit matters most.
- A network-dependent navigation is not a reliable native signal. Probe and
  fall back to a no-network URL that preserves the origin and per-open token.
- Keep the decision logic in a dependency-free core module when the native
  bundle cannot be imported by tests. The shell file should be thin effect
  wiring; that makes the security check unit-testable without Capacitor.
